scope: Independent recovery of the original completed browser comparison; no application or benchmark was rerun.

environment.renderer: Uno shared WebGPU / SwiftShader Vulkan software adapter

protocol.median: upper middle sorted sample at floor(n/2)
protocol.p95: nearest rank ceil(n * .95); with 16 samples this is the maximum observed sample

endpointProjectionEqualityScope: Full uniform, terrain-transform and eye payload equality is verified only for the untimed before/after SceneProjection captures.

additionalTimedStepSceneMetadata.scope: Only the lastDiagnostic metadata/count fields for each paired serialized step are compared. This does not verify full submitted matrices, terrain-transform words or geometry hashes for intermediate timed frames.

limitations: SwiftShader Vulkan software-adapter results do not establish hardware-GPU or display FPS, physical display latency or mobile thermals.
Serialized steps include a queue-completion and quiet-time barrier; their queue callback latency is not a GPU timestamp or sustained throughput.

Full camera/projection/terrain-transform payload parity is captured only at untimed before/after endpoints. Matching timed-step diagnostic metadata/counts does not establish equality of every intermediate submitted matrix or geometry payload.
No scenario is entirely free of texture uploads/resource allocation. The three map cases have 12/16 warm steps per variant; paused walking/look has 0/16.
The four moving windows have only 2–4 actual map submissions and multi-second initial/final queue backlog. Report them individually rather than asserting a robust large throughput gain.
CDP main-thread totals are retained as reported. Original before/after CDP metric snapshots are absent, so those totals cannot be independently rederived.
Page-error absence is a successful source-harness assertion; the original per-page exception event list is not retained in raw records.
